title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
abstract: arXiv:2610.32051v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. translated_title: 利比里亚社区卫生计划中药物“最后一公里”配送的动态库存配给模型
translated_abstract: 我们研究利比里亚社区卫生计划中稀缺药物的动态分配问题。一个中央仓库为一家卫生机构及其所监管的社区卫生助理（CHAs）供应药品。当社区卫生助理的药品耗尽时，患者会被转诊至该卫生机构——若患者完成转诊则产生交通成本，否则将得不到治疗。将库存分配给社区卫生助理可以让更多患者无需出行即可获得治疗，而将库存集中保留在中央仓库则保留了应对不确定需求的灵活性。这一分配问题必须在权衡上述因素的同时兼顾各地点之间的公平性。我们将该问题表述为一个有限时域的随机控制问题，其目标函数综合了转诊成本、患者未接受治疗的成本以及按需求加权的公平性效用。由于标准的动态规划方法在此情境下计算上不可行，我们开发了一种连续时间（方法）……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将利比里亚社区卫生计划中稀缺药物的动态分配问题建模为有限时域随机控制问题，在转诊成本、患者未治疗成本与地区间公平性之间取得平衡，以解决“将库存下放给社区卫生助理”与“集中保留库存以应对不确定需求”之间的权衡难题。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates the dynamic rationing of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem that balances referral and untreated-patient costs with demand-weighted fairness, addressing the trade-off between distributing inventory to Community Health Assistants and retaining central flexibility under uncertain demand.
